Skip to main content Russia-China Cooperation in the Energy Sector as a Platform for Innovation, Resilience, and Technological Sovereignty Published: 21 November 2026 Volume 18 , article number 9 ( 2027 ) Cite this article View saved research Journal of the Knowledge Economy Aims and scope Submit manuscript Abstract Russia-China energy cooperation is usually analyzed through commercial or geopolitical lenses, leaving unclear whether long-term energy interdependence can function as a platform for knowledge creation, diffusion, and application. In this paper, instead of treating energy infrastructure as purely commercial or geopolitical asset, the authors examine whether these linkages can operate as knowledge infrastructures that enable learning and innovation. The analysis combines a review of literature, a qualitative case study of hydrocarbon and electricity cooperation, indicator triangulation from policy and industry sources, and scenario analysis. The paper develops a multi-level framework in which energy interdependence affects knowledge creation and diffusion through five operationally connected mechanisms: infrastructure commitment, joint engineering projects, standards and settlement, logistics data, and human-capital mobility. Results show that the cooperation is strongest as a risk-management and market-redirecting mechanism, but weaker as a generator of endogenous innovation because asymmetries in bargaining power, sanctions exposure, localization incentives, and Russia’s raw-material bias constrain learning. The authors develop four scenarios of Russia-China cooperation in the energy sector to demonstrate that the developmental value of energy interdependence depends on the speed of the energy transition and the degree of geopolitical fragmentation.
